## Why visit

One of the most memorable small pub buildings in either city: a green-tiled wedge standing apart from the surrounding development. The interior rewards a slow look through the drinking lobby, snug and other little rooms, with stained glass, woodwork and old seating. Its relatively focused cask selection suits the setting; this is a place to appreciate a well-kept familiar beer and the pub around it. Pair it with Britons Protection for two very different examples of Manchester’s surviving drinking-room traditions.

## Beer

CAMRA documents four regular cask ales, including regional beer and established classics; the listed range includes Titanic Plum Porter and Timothy Taylor Landlord. CAMRA additionally lists Millstone Tiger Rut and Brightside The Mancunian as regulars alongside Titanic Plum Porter and Timothy Taylor Landlord.

## Plan the visit

CAMRA reports a longstanding Tuesday Irish music session; check directly if planning around it. Narrow passages are part of the historic layout.

**Getting there:** Walk from Manchester Oxford Road or St Peter’s Square; very close to Britons Protection.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
